newsitem.title: USA: Alliant Techsystems wins $2 mln contract.
newsitem.headline: Alliant Techsystems wins $2 mln contract.

text.p: Alliant Techsystems Inc said Monday its aerospace systems group has been awarded a contract valued at $2 million from Raytheon Co.
The contract covers a system to be used in Raytheon's Aircraft Beech/Pilatus PC-9 MkII(TM), an airplane that will be used to train U.S. Air Force and U.S. Navy pilots into the next century.
The contract contains production options for 141 Laser Canopy Fracturing Initiation Systems.

The Beech MkII was the winning entry in a Joint Primary Aircraft Training System (JPATS) program, which involves the production of up to 711 training aircraft through the year 2017 under a $4 billion program. Seven aircraft companies participated in the competition.

Alliant's Laser Canopy Fracturing Initiation System uses fiber optic cable and laser technology to initiate the explosive system that fractures the aircraft canopy before the pilot's ejection seat passes through it. Unlike explosive transfer lines currently used for ejection systems, the fiber optic cables used by Alliant's system do not have to be replaced periodically.
